text:
Yes. A **full switch** to Monzo through the UK’s Current Account Switch Service moves your existing Direct Debits automatically. **Don’t cancel or recreate them.** The switch also moves your standing orders and remaining balance, redirects incoming payments such as your salary, and **closes your old account**. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/switch?utm_source=openai))

1. **Open a Monzo current account** if you don’t already have one. Check that Monzo and your old bank have the same address for you. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/current-account/personal?utm_source=openai))
2. **Start the switch in the Monzo app:** go to **Home → the three dots on your account → Switch to Monzo**. Follow the prompts and choose a switch date at least **7 working days** away. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/switch?utm_source=openai))
3. **Keep enough money in your old account** for bills due before the switch date. If you need to set up a *new* Direct Debit during those final 7 working days, use your **Monzo** details. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/switch?utm_source=openai))

**One exception:** subscriptions charged to your **debit card number** aren’t Direct Debits. Update those with the provider using your new Monzo card details. If an actual Direct Debit is missing after the switch, contact Monzo; the Switch Guarantee covers charges or interest caused by a switching error. ([nationwide.co.uk](https://www.nationwide.co.uk/-/assets/nationwidecouk/documents/current-accounts/resources/p2205-switching-guide.pdf?rev=2d10426b78fb44d39f7ab3a2346395f2&utm_source=openai))
